summary: Joseph Margolis (1924–2021) was a philosopher who earned his M.A. at Columbia University (~1948–1950). He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University in 1991 and taught Youru Wang.

Joseph Marino works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington (attested 2013–2017), studying under doctoral supervisor Richard Salomon and teacher Collett Cox.

Joseph Needham (1900–1995) worked in Sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Cambridge (~1918–1924), he was a Fellow (~1924–1995) and Master (~1966–1976) of Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge Reader in Biochemistry (~1933–1966), and Director of the Needham Research Institute (~1987–1990).

Joseph Prabhu works in philosophy and religious studies, having studied under Bernard Williams. He held posts at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007) and was a visiting professor at institutions including United Theological College, Bangalore, and UC Santa Barbara.

Joseph Ratzinger (1927–2022) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher. Educated at the University of Munich (~1947–1951) and Ducal Georgianum (1949–1951), he held professorial posts at Munich, Bonn, Münster, Tübingen (~1966–1969), and Regensburg (~1969–1977).

Joseph Rock (1884–1962) was a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology. He taught at Mid-Pacific Institute and Mills Institute (~1908), served as botanist and curator at the University of Hawaiʻi (1908, 1911–1920), and worked for the USDA (~1920–1924).
Joseph Tiefenthaler (1710–1785) was an Indologist and historian who served as a Jesuit missionary in the Society of Jesus from 1729 to 1773 and held the post of Rector at St. Peter's College, Agra.

Joseph Toussaint Reinaud (1795–1867) was a historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Silvestre de Sacy. He was curator of Oriental manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and professor of Arabic at INALCO from 1838.

Joseph Vendryes (1875–1960) was a linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1907–1946), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1907–1946), and École Normale Supérieure (~1907–1914).

Joseph Walser is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied under Isshi Yamada, Adolf von Wuertenburg, and David S. Pacini. He held an attested post at Loyola University Chicago in 1998.

Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall (1774–1856) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic history. He studied at the K.k. Akademie für Orientalische Sprachen (~1789–1799) and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1847–1849).
Josho Nozawa (1906–1968) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1950).
Joshua Marshman (1768–1837) was an Indologist and Sinologist. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua T. Katz (1969–) is a linguist educated at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1998). He was Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute (~2022).
Joshua W. C. Cutler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Wangyal and was affiliated with the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center (attested 2004).

Josiah Royce (1855–1916) was an American philosopher educated at UC Berkeley, Göttingen (under Hermann Lotze), and Johns Hopkins. After teaching at Berkeley (~1878–1882), he served on the Harvard University faculty from 1882 to 1916.

Jost Gippert (1956–) is a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies who studied at the University of Marburg (~1972–1977). He served as Director of the Institute for Empirical Linguistics at Goethe University Frankfurt (1994–2022).

José Ignacio Cabezón (1956–) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Caltech, Sera, and UW–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He taught at Iliff School of Theology (~1990–2001) before becoming Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London (attested 2012) under the supervision of Kate Crosby.

Jowita Kramer (1974–) is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Hamburg and Munich. She taught at Munich (2017–2021) before becoming professor and head of the Institute for Indology and Central Asian Studies at Leipzig in 2021.
